# `silk/text/utf8_scan`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Random-access decoding of one Unicode scalar from UTF-8 bytes, for text algorithms that scan by
byte offset.

## When to use
Use [`decode`](#decode) in a hot loop that keeps byte offsets, such as a segmentation or line breaking
scan. Use `String.nextScalar` in `silk.text.string` for ordinary iteration over a `string`, and
`silk.text.utf8_decoder` for bytes that arrive in pieces.

## Details
[`decode`](#decode) reads the scalar at a byte offset and gives the offset after it. It accepts only the
well-formed sequences of RFC 3629. An ill-formed byte, or a sequence that ends early, gives
U+FFFD and moves one byte, so a scan always moves forward. The function does not allocate.

## Examples
### Decode the scalars of a byte string
```silk
import silk.text.utf8_scan

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let bytes = b"a\xc3\xa9\xff"
  let first = utf8_scan.decode(bytes, 0)
  let second = utf8_scan.decode(bytes, first.next)
  let third = utf8_scan.decode(bytes, second.next)
  if first.scalar != 0x61 || second.scalar != 0xe9 || third.scalar != 0xfffd || third.next != 4 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `utf8_scan` with `import silk.text.utf8_scan as utf8_scan`.

<a id="decode"></a>

## `decode`

```silk
pub fn decode(bytes: &[u8], at: usize) -> Decoded
```

Decodes the UTF-8 scalar that starts at byte offset `at` of `bytes`.

### Details

A well-formed sequence gives its scalar and the offset after it. An ill-formed byte, an
overlong form, a surrogate, a value past U+10FFFF, or a sequence that ends early gives U+FFFD
and `at + 1`. At or past the end of `bytes`, the result is U+FFFD and the length of `bytes`.
ASCII decodes inline; longer sequences take one call.
